newsitem.title: USA: Cross Timbers sets cash flow and cost goals.
newsitem.headline: Cross Timbers sets cash flow and cost goals.

text.p: Cross Timbers Oil Co said Tuesday it aims to increase cash flow to $4.45 per share in 1998 and $5.50 in 1999, an aggregate increase of 50 percent from this year's goal of $3.67.

With the recent completion of a $39.5 million acquisition, it said it expects to meet its previously announced cash flow goal for 1997, assuming continued drilling success and current commodity prices.
Cross Timbers said it expects annual exploration and development costs of $70-$90 million in both 1998 and 1999, depending on drilling results, property acquisitions and commodity prices.
Higher-risk expenditures, including step-out development and exploratory drilling, are targeted to be up to 20 of total costs, it said.
The company said it plans to make strategic acquisitions totaling $260-$280 million between now and the end of 1999.
Cross Timbers expects development costs to be funded from cash flow, while acquisitions and stock repurchases will be funded with a combination of cash flow and debt, it said.
The company said it may repurchase up to 1.6 million shares of common that remain available under its current repurchase authorization.
